Real browser search row IDs/timestamps/full content/total match the independently collected WARN and separate authenticated GET for every boundary.
checklist_items.16.8: Read actual downloaded CSV bytes, UTF-8 and schema, compare every field to loaded rows

checklist_items.2.1: PARTIAL: initial query/instance/node values, placeholders, enabled/optional/single-line metadata are observed; full persistent accessible labels remain a product gap. Placeholders do not substitute for labels.
checklist_items.2.6: Covered: actual clipboard permissions and Control+V populate query/instance/node-search inputs, Control+A/Backspace clear each, exact browser GET parameters and known hit/empty results match. Editing sends zero mutation requests; final independent GET and UI filter state restore the original WARN. Multiline is inapplicable to these single-line controls.
checklist_items.18.8: Covered: real browser text-first and chips-first paths use one/two quick terms, exact grouped text AND (WARNING OR ERROR), phrase quotes and free-text OR; search and histogram queries and known hit/empty results match. Removing matching/nonmatching chips and clearing restore the exact original text result.
checklist_items.16.7: covered: the export is consumed as a finished file rather than as a click. The real download event is awaited, its failure() must be None, the bytes are saved to disk and re-read, and they are parsed with the standard csv module independently of the product's serializer - so the check is against the delivered artefact, not the component that produced it. The bytes are then proven to carry the actual UTF-8 and CSV escaping markers, the filename keeps its gpuworks-logs-*.csv contract, and the sha256 of what landed on disk is recorded as the evidence.
checklist_items.2.4: covered: the keyword control is asserted on what it sends, not on what it displays. Four character shapes are typed and the query that reaches the server is compared exactly - Chinese text, a punctuation run of colon, quotes, parentheses, brackets and braces, a string carrying percent, ampersand and equals so the encoder has something to get wrong, and a two-line value. Each is then read back through the response, and the run returns to a matching keyword afterwards so the export that follows is not silently disabled by a probe. The single-line control is required to collapse the newline rather than truncate at it or keep a character the field cannot represent, and the Chinese and punctuation values are required to arrive unchanged. No character is forbidden by this field: the server accepts every shape and answers with the empty result set, which is recorded as the contract rather than as a failure. Proven by mutation: stripping non-ASCII characters from the query fails the Chinese case as the request never matches what the browser was told to send.
checklist_items.2.7: covered: a log line is rendered as text, and that is asserted rather than assumed. A warning whose stored line carries markup - a bold element, a script element that would set a global, an escaped ampersand and an image element with an inline handler - is collected through the same real server selflog route as every other fixture row, and the stored line is required to still contain that markup unchanged, so an entity doubling on the way in would fail before rendering is even reached. The row is then searched for through the box with the server source selected, and the rendering is measured: an element whose textContent is the whole line is required to exist, the row's own container is required to contain no b, script or img element, and the global the script would set is required to be absent - so markup becoming DOM, or a handler executing, fails here. Proven by mutation: rendering the highlighted segment with dangerouslySetInnerHTML fails as no element's textContent equals the line any more.
checklist_items.2.3: covered: the page size is the field with a length contract on this surface, and the four values around its thresholds are sent rather than one comfortable middle value. Below the floor - 0 - is required to be clamped up to the default, which exceeds the match count and so returns every match; at the floor - 1 - exactly one row is required back and the page is required to mark itself truncated, because more matches wait behind it; at the ceiling - 5000 - everything is required back and the page is required not to claim truncation, since nothing is being hidden; above the ceiling - 5001 - is required to be clamped down and answered without an error. Counting is in whole rows, which is the unit the endpoint documents, and the credential and time fields are strings with no length contract of their own, which is recorded rather than invented. The truncation half is what makes the floor case meaningful: only a page that came back full while matches remain may carry the marker. Proven by mutation: removing the store's one-row lookahead makes the floor case return a full page without marking it truncated.

time_semantics: Both endpoints included: known real WARN tested at exact lower/upper timestamps and excluded one millisecond beyond each endpoint.
export_contract: Current loaded entries, not all backend matches. BOM is optional because the product does not promise it.
cleanup: Stop only the owned LocalServer and release its port lock; preserve the private run database/logs for diagnosis, with seven-day scoped removal guidance. No shared server, GPU, agent or Docker dependency.
